messages.author: 4184023bb084c468
messages.subject: purl() produces png/X11 warning
parts:
Hi,

I ran purl() on a document:

> library(knitr)

> purl("cloudeqtl.Rmd")

Warning in png(tempfile()) :

  unable to open connection to X11 display ''

Note the warning that it emitted.


Questions:

1) Why that warning? Did purl() actually evaluate code? I thought it was just writing the code chunks to a .R file?

2) Does it matter? Do I need to worry that my R file is not complete somehow? Note that I don't care at this point if knit() would not work because of the X11/png() issue; I just want to know if I can trust purl() in this case.


Thanks,

Dan

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] purl() produces png/X11 warning
parts:
It does not matter. It comes from a test of the availability of the
png() device, and it turns out that png() does not seem to be
available on your platform. From my experience, the most likely reason
is that you built R from source, but did not install the pango
headers, so R does not have full cairo support, and png() has to fall
back to X11, which is not available, either.

Regards,
Yihui
